FINAL FIX — REPAIR IVX OWNER AUTHORIZATION AND COMPLETE DEPLOYMENT

Do not ask the owner to paste the old static IVX token again.

The audit has confirmed:

- IVX_OWNER_TOKEN is missing from the Rork runtime.
- The current production worker does not accept the static owner token.
- backend/api/owner-only.ts requires a Supabase owner JWT.
- Public chat still returns HTTP 409.
- The latest chat fix is not deployed.
- Production deployment authorization is blocked.

The correct fix is to implement one secure authentication path end to end.

==================================================
1. STOP USING THE STATIC TOKEN AS A SUPABASE JWT
==================================================

The existing 64-character IVX owner token is not a Supabase JWT.

Do not send it through:

Authorization: Bearer <static-token>

if backend/api/owner-only.ts validates Supabase JWTs.

Do not weaken the owner JWT guard.

Do not bypass owner authorization globally.

==================================================
2. IMPLEMENT SERVER-TO-SERVER DEPLOYMENT AUTH
==================================================

Create a separate internal deployment authentication mechanism for IVX autonomous workers.

Use secure environment variables:

IVX_INTERNAL_DEPLOY_SECRET
IVX_INTERNAL_WORKER_ID

Store them only in:

- Render production environment
- Rork secure project environment
- Approved IVX worker environment

Do not expose them in frontend code.
Do not commit them to GitHub.
Do not print their values in logs.

Generate a new high-entropy secret.

The worker request must send:

X-IVX-Worker-ID: <worker-id>
X-IVX-Deploy-Signature: <HMAC signature>
X-IVX-Timestamp: <unix timestamp>
X-IVX-Nonce: <unique nonce>

The backend must verify:

- Worker ID matches.
- Timestamp is recent.
- Nonce has not been reused.
- HMAC signature is valid.
- Request body has not been modified.
- Requested action is an allowed deployment action.
- Owner approval record exists for production deployment.

Reject with:

401 for missing or invalid authentication.
403 for authenticated but unauthorized requests.
409 only for a real deployment-state conflict.

Do not return HTTP 409 for missing credentials.

==================================================
3. KEEP NORMAL OWNER LOGIN ON SUPABASE JWT
==================================================

Human owner authentication must continue using Supabase Auth.

Owner browser/mobile flow:

1. Owner signs in using email and password.
2. Supabase returns a valid access-token JWT.
3. Owner requests use:

Authorization: Bearer <Supabase access token>

4. Backend validates JWT.
5. Backend verifies the authenticated user is the approved IVX owner.

Do not replace normal owner login with the internal deploy secret.

The system must have two separate paths:

A. Human owner:
Supabase JWT

B. Authorized autonomous worker:
Signed internal server-to-server authentication

==================================================
4. ADD OWNER APPROVAL RECORD
==================================================

Production deployments must require an owner approval record.

Create or verify a table such as:

owner_deployment_approvals

Required fields:

- id
- owner_user_id
- requested_commit_sha
- action
- status
- approved_at
- expires_at
- used_at
- request_id
- created_at

Rules:

- Approval is single-use.
- Approval expires.
- Commit SHA must match the approved commit.
- Deployment action must match the approved action.
- Worker cannot deploy a different commit.
- Replayed approvals must be rejected.

==================================================
5. UPDATE THE WORKER ROUTE
==================================================

Audit and update:

backend/api/owner-only.ts
render.yaml
worker deployment code
chat deployment action
production deployment endpoint

The endpoint must support:

- Supabase owner JWT for direct owner actions.
- Signed worker authentication for autonomous execution.
- Owner approval validation before production mutation.

Do not remove existing owner authorization protections.

Return:

- Exact files changed.
- Exact authentication flow.
- Exact environment variable names.
- No secret values.

==================================================
6. UPDATE RENDER CONFIGURATION
==================================================

Add the new secure variables to the correct Render services:

- Production API
- Senior worker
- Any autonomous deployment worker

Verify by service ID, not service display name only.

Return:

Service:
Environment variable:
PRESENT / MISSING
Loaded at startup:
YES / NO

Do not expose values.

The variables must be explicitly bound in render.yaml or the correct Render environment group.

Do not assume my-env-group contains the variables.

==================================================
7. FIX RENDER.YAML
==================================================

Update render.yaml so the API and worker receive the correct secret environment variables.

Audit the current configuration around:

- render.yaml lines 34–146
- render.yaml lines 202–225
- environment group import
- API service definition
- worker service definition

Confirm both services load the required values.

Do not create another Render service.

Do not create another repository.

Use the existing production services.

==================================================
8. FIX CHAT HTTP 409
==================================================

The public chat must not return HTTP 409 because the deployment worker is unauthorized.

Separate chat rendering from deployment authorization.

Expected behavior:

- Normal chat request returns HTTP 200 with a renderable answer.
- Deployment request without authorization returns HTTP 401 or 403.
- Deployment request with valid authorization and owner approval executes.
- Real state conflicts may return HTTP 409 with a structured reason.

Return the exact source of the current HTTP 409 and fix it.

==================================================
9. TEST LOCALLY
==================================================

Run all tests before production deployment.

Required tests:

1. Owner JWT valid:
Expected 200

2. Owner JWT invalid:
Expected 401

3. Non-owner JWT:
Expected 403

4. Worker signature valid plus owner approval:
Expected authorized execution

5. Worker signature missing:
Expected 401

6. Worker signature invalid:
Expected 401

7. Expired timestamp:
Expected 401

8. Reused nonce:
Expected 401

9. Missing owner approval:
Expected 403

10. Approved commit does not match requested commit:
Expected 403

11. Public chat:
Expected HTTP 200 and renderable answer

12. Deployment conflict:
Expected structured HTTP 409 only when a real conflict exists

==================================================
10. DEPLOY THE CURRENT FIX
==================================================

After tests pass:

- Commit the authentication fix.
- Push to ibb142/rork-global-real-estate-invest.
- Confirm current GitHub main HEAD.
- Deploy the latest commit to the existing Render service.
- Do not deploy an older commit.
- Restart the API and worker so environment variables load.
- Verify no stale container remains.

==================================================
11. PRODUCTION VERIFICATION
==================================================

Return this evidence:

AUTHENTICATION PROOF

Owner Supabase JWT path:
PASS / FAIL

Internal worker signed-auth path:
PASS / FAIL

Owner approval validation:
PASS / FAIL

Replay protection:
PASS / FAIL

Unauthorized request rejection:
PASS / FAIL

DEPLOYMENT PROOF

GitHub repository:
Branch:
GitHub HEAD SHA:
Render service ID:
Render deployment ID:
Render live commit SHA:
Deployment status:
Deployment timestamp:

API PROOF

/health status:
Health response:
Live commit:
Version:
Boot time:

CHAT PROOF

Public-chat HTTP status:
Renderable response:
Previous HTTP 409 fixed:
YES / NO

WORKER PROOF

Worker authentication:
PASS / FAIL

Owner approval consumed:
YES / NO

Authorized deployment execution:
PASS / FAIL

==================================================
FINAL PASS CONDITIONS
==================================================

Mark COMPLETE only when:

- Owner login uses a valid Supabase JWT.
- Autonomous worker uses secure signed server-to-server authentication.
- Production deployment still requires owner approval.
- No static token is incorrectly treated as a JWT.
- Render API and worker load their secure variables.
- Current GitHub commit is live.
- Render deployment succeeds.
- /health returns HTTP 200.
- Public chat returns HTTP 200 with a renderable response.
- Deployment requests return correct 401, 403, or 409 statuses.
- Evidence includes commit SHA, deployment ID, logs, and timestamps.

Do not ask the owner for another token until this authentication architecture is implemented and tested.
